test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements about the centre of curvature of a spherical mirror is NOT true?

options.text: It lies outside the reflecting surface of the mirror.
For a concave mirror, it is located behind the mirror.
It is not a part of the mirror itself.
For a convex mirror, it lies behind the mirror.

solution:
The correct answer is __**For a concave mirror, it is located behind the mirror.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **centre of curvature** of a spherical mirror is defined as the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part. It is represented by the letter **C**.
 
• **Statement 1:** It lies outside the reflecting surface of the mirror. **This statement is correct** because the center of curvature is always located at a point outside the mirror, on the principal axis.
 
• **Statement 2:** For a concave mirror, it is located behind the mirror. **This statement is incorrect** as the center of curvature for a concave mirror lies in front of the reflecting surface, not behind it.
 
• **Statement 3:** It is not a part of the mirror itself. **This statement is correct** since the center of curvature is a geometric point and does not lie on the mirror's surface
